_comment: Guided tour of the phasor-FLIM tool in the emtk window. Steps point at real controls and wait for the user to use them.

steps.title: What this tool computes
steps.text: A phasor is a fit-free lifetime readout: each pixel's decay becomes a point (g, s) on a plane. Single-exponential decays sit on the universal semicircle (short lifetimes right, long ones left); mixtures fall inside it. You press the buttons; the tour only points at them.

steps.title: Choose the photon file
steps.text: A PTU or HT3 file with line and frame markers. Type a path and press Enter, press Browse or Database, or drop a file on the window.

await.hint: Select a photon file. Nothing is computed until you press Run.

steps.title: Frequency and minimum photons
steps.text: The frequency is the modulation frequency the phasor is taken at (-1 reads it from the file header); Min photons discards pixels too dim for a meaningful phasor. A changed value needs a new Run.

steps.title: Compute
steps.text: Run computes one phasor map per detector window in the background. A calibrated phasor needs the instrument response: IRF reference takes it per window (inside the Imaging Tools pipeline it comes from the IRF & BG step).

await.hint: Press Run and wait until the status line is empty.

steps.title: The phasor plot
steps.text: Every pixel is a point; the colour is how many fall in a bin. The semicircle is the universal circle. Add an ellipse or polygon cursor in the list below the settings and drag its handles round a cluster.

steps.title: Back to the image
steps.text: The Selected tab shows the intensity of the pixels inside the cursors: the image gated by lifetime. Invert selects everything outside a cursor.

steps.title: Write the result
steps.text: Add phasor to HDF5 appends the g and s columns to the pipeline's imaging HDF5 (or asks for a file); Save container, ndX and Next work as in the other per-pixel tools.

await.hint: Press Add phasor to HDF5 and choose a file name.
